title: Dashboard linting and template primer for inference metrics
body:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a lightweight "dashboard linting" approach and a small set of dashboard templates for inference stacks. Goal: make dashboards repeatable, low-cost, and reviewable as part of model rollouts and canary experiments. We want a CI-friendly checklist that catches high-cardinality panels, unbounded label explosion, expensive queries, and panels that are ambiguous for oncall.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to service-level and model-level dashboards for hosted/dedicated/private inference routes.
- Focus on tokenized-generation, KV cache, routing/fallbacks, and embedding endpoints.
- We do not prescribe specific visual styles; we focus on query safety, metric contracts, and templating variables.

High-level rules (dashboard linting):
1) Naming and description for each panel: short title + 1-line description of signal and investigatory use (why).
2) Metric contracts attached as annotations: expected unit, aggregation (sum/count/gauge), cardinality hints for labels (low/medium/high).
3) Query cost ceiling: queries evaluated in <500ms on sampling cluster. If not, add sampled backend or materialized rollup.
4) Cardinality guard rails: no panel should expand into more than 25 series by default. If it can, default to topk(10) and provide drilldown template.
5) Label hygiene: prohibit free-text label grouping for high-cardinality fields (prompt_text, user_message_id). Use hashed or bucketed labels when needed.
6) Rate-limited live queries: any panel that executes per-dashboard-load must have a query-time limit and feature a cached rollup.
7) SLO linkage: every rollout dashboard must include an explicit SLO panel referencing the exact metrics and window used for decision-making.
8) Trace anchors: panels that show slow tails must include a linkable trace anchor (trace_id or session_id) and sampling guidance.

Metric lint checklist (to run in CI or during PR):
- All metrics used by panels exist in metric catalog and have canonical names.
- Units present for all numeric axes.
- aggregation is explicit (e.g., rate(token_count[1m]) / sum(token_count) is discouraged; prefer rate(token_count_total[1m]) with defined denominator).
- Avoid doing joins at presentation time that cause cross-tenant leakage.
- Ensure tenancy filters or panel template variables are present for multi-tenant views.

Suggested templating variables (minimal set):
- tenant_id (optional)
- model_name
- model_version
- route_name
- window (1m/5m/1h)
- environment (prod/stage/canary)
These should drive panel filters and allow a single dashboard to support per-tenant, per-model drills.

Standard panel templates (text sketches):
- SLO Summary (compact): shows error-rate, 99p latency TTF token, success_rate, and budget remaining. Text: "SLOs: err% (1h), 99p_lat_ttf (30m), budget".
- Latency Heatmap by token position: 2D heatmap (token position vs p50/p95 latency). Use pre-aggregated histograms to avoid expensive group_by.
- KV Warmth and Prefetch Impact: panel with kv_cache_hit_rate, kv_evictions, and a derived prefetch_effectiveness metric computed server-side.
- Cost-per-1k-tokens lane: show cpu/gpu-time-per-token, average tokens-per-request, and effective $/1k tokens. Use sampled billing rollups not raw traces.
- Error breakout by failure-class: mapping to upstreams (model OOM, timeout, api-rate-limit, user-error). Limit series to first 8 classes.
- Trace-sampled slow-path links: table of sample traces for slow requests with sample probability and link to trace viewer.

Tracing guidance and anchors:
- Define "trace anchors" for inference flows: request_received -> auth -> routing -> model_infer_start -> model_infer_end -> response_sent. Each anchor should have a standard span name.
- Sampling policies:
  - Always sample 1/1000 of requests for full traces (baseline).
  - Always sample 100% of requests failing SLO or returning 5xx for 5m after failure burst.
  - Adaptive sampling for slow tails: increase sample rate for traces in 95-99.9p latency windows.
- Enrich traces with: tenant_id (hashed), model_name, model_version, route_name, request_token_count, and kv_warmth_flag. Do not record raw prompt or PII in traces.
- Trace retention tiers: full traces for 7d, metadata-only for 90d. Add step to scrub PHI/PII prior to tiering.

Dashboard cost & query budget advice:
- Prefer rollup tables for wholesale aggregations (per-model 1m rollup stored in a materialized table).
- Use sampled dashboards for heavy histogram visualizations. Provide a debug toggle to re-run with full queries only for oncall.
- Allocate a per-dashboard query budget (e.g., 50ms * 10 panels per load) and monitor consumption. If exceeded, convert offending panels to cached snapshots.

Oncall-readiness and quick investigation notes (for each dashboard PR include):
- Quick links at top to: tracing explorer, recent incident runbook, canary experiment page.
- An investigations cheat-sheet (2–3 targeted first questions):
  1) Is the degradation isolated to tenants or global? (check tenant filter + top-10 by traffic)
  2) Is it cold-start/KV-warmth related? (kv_hit_rate over the time window)
  3) Is a model switch/rollout correlated? (model_version changes + deploy timestamps)
- Add a single-sentence remediation suggestion for each critical panel (e.g., "If 99p latency > threshold: switch to fallback model immediately and warm KV cache by running prefetch job.").

CI integration for dashboard PRs (minimal):
- Lint step validates: panel titles, metric existence, cardinality guards, presence of SLO panel, and templating variables coverage.
- Cost estimation step: run sample queries on a small dataset and estimate average query wall time. Fail PR if any panel exceeds 500ms cost threshold.
- Automated smoke snapshot: render panels with synthetic 30m data and check for NaNs/missing series.

Rollout checklist (for model rollouts using templated dashboards):
- Attach dashboard PR to rollout ticket and include reviewers from eng-observability and model-owner.
- Verify that SLO thresholds are present and agreed upon in the ticket.
- Create canary probe (synthetic requests) tied to the dashboard SLOs and ensure traces are sampled for canary traffic.
- Run smoke queries and confirm dashboard loads under budget.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- How strict should linting be vs team autonomy? Propose: must-fix for cardinality and cost items; warnings for style.
- What is the right default cardinality cap? We suggest 25 series by default but are open to 50 for specialized panels.
- Where to host materialized rollups for private deployments? Options: customer's datalake vs Redwood-managed aggregated store.

Next steps / action items:
- Prototype a Grafana dashboard linter using our JSON model and run against 50 existing dashboards by Feb 2026. Owner: Ethan Rivera.
- Draft a lightweight metric-contract template YAML and land it in github.com/redwood-inference/metric-catalog. Owner: Priya Nair.
- Ship a dashboard PR checklist template and include it in the rollout playbook. Owner: Maya Chen.

Appendix: quick metric-name guard examples:
- Good: inference.request.duration_ms{model_name,model_version,env} (gauge, unit ms, cardinality low)
- Bad: inference.request.duration_ms{prompt_text} (free-text label -> reject)
- Good: inference.kv.cache_hit_rate{model_name} (percentage, rollup 1m)

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally prescriptive but minimal. The intent is to stop the most costly and ambiguous dashboard anti-patterns while keeping teams empowered to design panels they need. Feedback appreciated, esp. on default cardinality and query-time thresholds.
